faqs.question: What is the effective tax rate in New York?
faqs.answer: It depends on your income level. New York state taxes are up to 10.9%, plus federal taxes and FICA.

faqs.question: How is effective tax rate different from marginal rate?
faqs.answer: Marginal rate is the tax on your last dollar of income. Effective rate is your total tax divided by total income — typically lower.

faqs.question: What taxes are included in the effective rate?
faqs.answer: Federal income tax, state income tax, Social Security tax (6.2%), and Medicare tax (1.45%).

faqs.question: How can I lower my effective tax rate?
faqs.answer: Maximize pre-tax deductions (401k, HSA), itemize deductions, use tax credits, and consider tax-loss harvesting.

faqs.question: Does New York have local income taxes too?
faqs.answer: Some New York localities may impose additional income taxes. Check with your city or county.
